newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hurricane Guillermo edges away from Mexican coast.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Guillermo edges away from Mexican coast.

text.p: Hurricane Guillermo gathered strength as it churned off Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday, but the powerful storm was expected to creep away from land, officials said.

Ports along Mexico's western coast were on high alert as the Pacific's warm waters strengthened the hurricane, which had sustained winds of 95 mph (150 kph) and gusts of up to 110 mph (175 kph), the National Meteorological Service said.
Guillermo was expected to pick up more strength later in the day, with wind gusts exceeding 120 mph (195 kph) and ocean swells reaching 13 feet (4 metres).
Officials said the storm was edging west, away from land, at 13 mph (20 kmh).
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), Guillermo was 410 miles (660 km) south-southwest of the port city and tourist resort of Manzanillo.
At 8 p.m. EDT (midnight GMT), the storm was expected to be 450 miles (725 km) southwest of Manzanillo, officials said.
